title: The All-Marquee Team
basis: 2026 preseason consensus, compiled before Week 1 kickoff. Companion to the all-city edition of the same week; same players, one extra rule.

rules.public_summary: Same rule as the All-City Team, one floor added: the city has to have had at least 100,000 residents at the 2020 census. Exact first or last name only, no nicknames, no partial matches, and the place still has to be a city rather than a town or a village.
rules.verification_note: Every population in the table is the 2020 census figure, checked 2026-08-31; Greater London is the 2024 estimate.
full_rules: The All-City rules apply in full: exact match on the player's own first or last name, whole tokens only, suffixes stripped, and the place must be classified a city.
Added floor: 100,000 residents at the 2020 census. This is the Marquee City tier from the parent edition, promoted from a label to the entry requirement.

The allied-cities clause now bites. Where no QUALIFYING U.S. city carries the name, a city of France, the United Kingdom or Sweden may be used. London, Ohio is 10,279 and fails the floor, so London means the other one.
For an allied city the class test is whether it is a city under its own country's usage and administration, because 'classified a city by its state' is a U.S. construct.
Washington runs on a named exception, written out under the table. The parent edition did not need one; at 100,000 it does.
considered_and_rejected: Dropping Washington entirely. Defensible on a strict reading, and it costs the roster 93 places of receiver (Parker Washington at overall 65 for Denzel Boston at 158) on a technicality about a jurisdiction everyone in the league has driven through. The exception is named and marked instead of hidden.
Refusing London. The four countries were in the premise from the start, and refusing the one time the clause has anything to say would make it decoration.
Metro-area population instead of city population. It would admit almost every name and delete the exercise.

cross_checks.label: Systematic pool sweep (2026-08-31)
cross_checks.finding: Rather than working from memory, every first and last name in the FantasyPros pool was intersected against the list of U.S. cities of 100,000 or more. 62 name matches surfaced across 371 candidate city names. The sweep changed nothing at QB, RB or TE and confirmed that the kicker pool is exactly two men, both named Tyler.

sources.label: London

starters.research_notes: The one and only time the allied-cities clause has decided anything. In the parent edition he qualified through London, Ohio (10,279) and still lost the slot to Chase and Jefferson; here the Ohio route fails the floor and the escalation clause hands him the far bigger city. Greater London is the administrative unit cited; the City of London is a separate square-mile corporation and is not what anybody means.

starters.exception: Washington, D.C. runs on a named exception. The Census Bureau's District of Columbia guide records that the District has one city, Washington, coextensive with it, and standard rankings of U.S. municipal corporations list Washington 22nd; the Bureau's population-estimates glossary treats the District as a county equivalent instead. The sources genuinely disagree, so this is a ruling rather than a reading.

sources.label: Washington, D.C.
sources.quote: Washington, D.C., officially the District of Columbia, is the federal capital city of the United States, and its only federal district. Population 689,545 at the 2020 census. The 1871 Organic Act made the city of Washington legally indistinguishable from the District of Columbia.

sources.label: Census Bureau geographic terms (population estimates glossary)
sources.quote: Incorporated places include cities, towns, boroughs, villages and other lesser known identifiers. The District of Columbia has no primary divisions and the jurisdiction is treated as the equivalent of a county.

sources.label: List of United States cities by population
sources.quote: This is a list of the most populous municipal corporations of the United States. Washington, DC appears at rank 22 with a 2020 population of 689,545.

starters.research_notes: The one discretionary call in the edition, and it is worth 93 places of receiver: without it the slot goes to Denzel Boston (Boston, 675,647) at overall 158, third on Cleveland's depth chart. Flagged in the table with a numbered footnote so a reader can disagree with it on the facts.
